properties.name: variant
properties.description:
Visual variant. Both share the same expand/collapse mechanics.
- `filled` (default) — each item is a tonal surface tile.
- `outlined` — items share a single rounded chassis with an outline.

properties.name: density
properties.description:
Density scale from `0` (default, 64 px minimum header) through `-4`
(48 px). Each rung reduces the minimum by 4 px; content may be taller.

properties.name: elevation
properties.description:
MD3 elevation level applied to the surface — `0` (default, flat)
through `5` (highest). In the `filled` variant each item gets its
own shadow; in the `outlined` variant the shadow is drawn on the
shared chassis. Expanded items lift to the next elevation level
for an expressive "lift off the page" affordance.

properties.name: reorderable
properties.description:
Allow drag-to-reorder of items via the leading drag handles. Items
can also be reordered with `Alt + ArrowUp / ArrowDown` while the
header is focused. Disabled items can't be moved.

properties.name: floating
properties.description:
Render the accordion as a free-floating panel that can be dragged
anywhere on the screen via the top drag-bar. The panel uses
`position: fixed` and translates via CSS transform, so it lifts
out of normal document flow.

properties.name: initialX
properties.description:
Initial X translation (px) for floating panels — measured in
PHYSICAL viewport coordinates from the top-left corner of the
viewport, so a positive value always moves the panel to the
right regardless of writing direction (LTR or RTL). Default: 24.

properties.name: initialY
properties.description:
Initial Y translation (px) for floating panels — measured in
physical viewport coordinates from the top-left corner. Default: 24.

properties.name: bringToFront
properties.description:
When a floating accordion starts being dragged, bring it to the
front by bumping `z-index`. Disable if you manage stacking
yourself.

properties.name: exclusive
properties.description:
Whether only one item may be expanded at a time. When `true`,
expanding an item collapses any other expanded item.

properties.name: keepOneExpanded
properties.description:
Require at least one item to remain expanded. APG variant: the
implementation does not permit the currently-open panel to be
collapsed when doing so would leave zero panels open. The locked-
open button advertises `aria-disabled="true"`. Pairs naturally
with `exclusive` to enforce "exactly one panel is always open".

properties.name: headingLevel
properties.description:
ARIA heading level for each item's heading wrapper (`<h1>`–`<h6>`).
Pick the value matching the page's information architecture — e.g.
`2` inside a top-level page section, `4` deep inside a card. APG:
"aria-level that is appropriate for the information architecture
of the page". Default `3`.

properties.name: region
properties.description:
Region-role policy for panels:
- `auto` (default) — applies `role="region"` only when the item
  count is at or below `region-threshold`, otherwise downgrades
  to `role="group"` to avoid landmark proliferation (per APG
  recommendation for accordions with more than ~6 panels).
- `always` — every panel is a landmark region.
- `never` — no panel carries a region role (still labelled via
  `aria-labelledby` though).

properties.name: regionThreshold
properties.description:
Threshold above which `region="auto"` downgrades panel roles
from `region` to `group`. APG suggests ~6.

properties.name: transition
properties.description:
Motion preset applied when items expand and collapse. The prop
is reflected so the item CSS can pick it up via
direct-owner presentation attributes on each item.

- `expressive` (default) — coordinated emphasized height and corner
   motion (350ms open / 250ms close), with spring-spatial chevron
   rotation and a leading-icon FILL-axis swap. Surface tone,
   opacity and elevation use shorter, non-overshooting effects.
   Content is revealed in place.
- `standard` — MD3 standard easing (symmetric `emphasized`) with
   no spring overshoot. Container morph still happens. The
   "neutral" preset — good default for dense product UI.
- `fade` — content fades in/out alongside the height animation
   using shorter `standard` easing. Chevron rotates without a
   spring. Best for content-heavy panels (forms, long copy)
   where the motion should be unobtrusive.
- `collapse` — height-led disclosure with `ease-out` on open and
   `ease-in` on close. Corners follow the same timing; no spring
   overshoot or content fade.
- `none` — disables every transition (instant snap). Useful for
   automated tests, screenshot harnesses, or environments where
   motion is undesirable.

properties.name: defaultExpanded
properties.description:
Comma-separated list of item indexes that should be expanded on
first render. Items with `expanded` set in their own attribute
also count.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Progressive disclosure for a set of sections. Groups md-accordion-item children, coordinates which are expanded, wires their heading level and panel roles, and adds optional drag/keyboard reordering plus a draggable floating panel mode.

notes: Dedicated native renderer: all fifteen properties, five events, the default slot and fourteen appearance hooks. Direct-child ownership, exclusive and keep-one coordination, heading/region presentation, pointer and keyboard reorder, lifted clipping, reorder motion, interaction states, drop-placeholder paint and the floating panel are checked against Chrome oracles.

Floating mode: the nearest awcAccordionViewport() or the window stands in for the CSS viewport. SwiftUI zIndex orders a panel only among siblings of its container, whereas CSS position: fixed stacks against the whole document.

drop-placeholder is rendered natively and styled through the five drop-placeholder appearance fields; native views accept no ::part declarations for it. The dash phase on sides after a rounded corner differs from Chrome by up to about one period (open).
macOS SwiftUI/AppKit renderer and live-host verification is recorded; iOS SDK, simulator/device and VoiceOver execution remain unavailable and unverified.

Direct-child ownership, exclusive and keep-one coordination, heading/region presentation, pointer and keyboard reorder, lifted clipping, reorder motion, interaction states, drop-placeholder paint and the floating panel are checked against Chrome oracles.

Floating mode: the nearest AWCAccordionViewport or the window root (insets are not subtracted) stands in for the CSS viewport. Compose zIndex orders a panel only among siblings of its container, whereas CSS position: fixed stacks against the whole document.

properties.name: headline
properties.description: Header text (or use the `headline` slot).

properties.name: supportingText
properties.description: Optional small caption below the headline.

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Optional leading-icon (Material Symbols shorthand).

properties.name: expanded
properties.description: Whether the item is expanded. Two-way bindable.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Disable interaction.

properties.name: headingLevel
properties.description:
ARIA heading level (`aria-level`) for the item's heading wrapper.
Renders a native `<h1>`–`<h6>` so the implicit semantics match the
page's information architecture. Per WAI-ARIA APG: "an element with
role heading that has a value set for aria-level that is
appropriate for the information architecture of the page".

Set per-item, or let the parent `<md-accordion heading-level>`
propagate the same value to every item.

properties.name: collapsible
properties.description:
Whether the item can be collapsed when it is expanded. Set to
`false` to implement the APG variant where the accordion does not
permit a panel to be collapsed — the open button then advertises
`aria-disabled="true"`, and Enter / Space / click no longer toggle
it. Typically managed by the parent's `keep-one-expanded` mode.

properties.name: regionRole
properties.description:
Role applied to the accordion panel. APG recommends `region` for
structural clarity, but warns against using it when more than ~6
panels can be open at once (landmark proliferation). The parent
`<md-accordion region>` orchestrates this automatically.

- `region` (default) — full landmark semantics.
- `group` — semantically a group but not a landmark.
- `none` — drop the role entirely (still labelled via aria-labelledby).

properties.name: contentMaxHeight
properties.description:
Cap the panel body's block-size (e.g. `"220px"`, `"40vh"`). When set,
the content region becomes a scroll container instead of growing to
fit — and, crucially, it is made keyboard-focusable (`tabindex="0"`)
so keyboard-only users can scroll it. A scrollable region whose
content isn't itself focusable is otherwise unreachable without a
pointer (WCAG 2.1.1 — axe `scrollable-region-focusable`). Its
accessible name comes from the enclosing labelled panel region.

Prefer this over hand-rolling a slotted `overflow:auto` wrapper: an
authored scroll `<div>` lives in light DOM the component can't make
focusable, so it would trip the same axe rule. Leave empty (default)
for a panel that grows to fit its content.

properties.name: density
properties.description:
Local density rung. Drives the same `--md-sys-density-scale` signal that a
global `data-density` ancestor sets, so a local value simply overrides the
inherited one. 0 = default, -4 = ultra-compact.

properties.name: variant
properties.description: Badge size — small renders a dot; large renders a label

properties.name: value
properties.description: Text or number to display (large variant only, max 4 visible characters)

properties.name: max
properties.description:
Numeric threshold. When the parsed value exceeds this, the badge
shows `{max}+` (e.g. `999+`). Ignored for non-numeric values.

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Material Symbols icon name (large variant only, e.g. `"error"`)

properties.name: shape
properties.description:
The SHAPE of the thing the badge is anchored to.

The badge pins to its containing block's top-inline-end CORNER and
translates itself onto it, which is right for a `rect` host — a button, a
tab, a tile. On a `circle` it is wrong for the same reason it is wrong for
`md-status-dot`: a circle's bounding-box corner lies outside the visible
shape, so the badge floats clear of the avatar with nothing behind it.

`circle` anchors it to the 45° point on the rim instead — the top-trailing
arc, where a count badge on an avatar belongs. Percentage insets, so it is
correct at every avatar size without being told the size, and it needs no
hand-tuned offsets at the call site.

`rect` stays the default: changing it would move every badge already
sitting on a button or a tab.

properties.name: density
properties.description:
Local density rung. Drives the same `--md-sys-density-scale` signal that a
global `data-density` ancestor sets, so a local value simply overrides the
inherited one. 0 = default, -4 = ultra-compact.

components.name: Badge
components.description: A small count or marker attached to another element. A dot, or a count pill. variant="small" is a bare dot for "something is here"; variant="large" is a pill carrying a number or a glyph. It positions itself absolutely at the upper-right corner of the nearest positioned ancestor — a physical anchor (top: 0; right: 0), which does not mirror in RTL — and never takes pointer events.

notes: Dedicated SwiftUI badge implements all six source properties, the authored icon slot and ten typed appearance hooks. awcBadgeOverlay uses the actual parent size for physical top-right rect/circle anchors; offsets combine native lengths with fractions of badge size. Explicit empty icon elements suppress fallback. Native layout and font rasterization replace CSS/browser rendering; runtime acceptance is recorded separately in the parity audit.

properties.name: subtitle

should not have to carry.

properties.name: titleAlign

properties.name: xAxis
properties.description: Category axis configuration.

properties.name: yAxis
properties.description: Value axis configuration.

properties.name: yAxis2
properties.description:
A SECOND value axis, drawn in the opposite gutter and used by any series
whose `yAxisIndex` is 1 — two quantities on one category axis that share no
scale, like a count and a rate. Vertical charts.

It draws no gridlines of its own: two sets at two spacings turn the plot
into a mesh nobody can read a value off.

properties.name: layout
properties.description: Bar layout — `'horizontal'` swaps categories onto the y axis.

properties.name: stack
properties.description: Stacking strategy: none (grouped) / normal / percentage.

properties.name: categoryGap
properties.description: Category gap as a percentage of the band width (`"30%"` or `30`).

properties.name: barGap
properties.description: Bar gap between sibling grouped bars (`"20%"` or `20`).

properties.name: barWidth
properties.description:
Fixed bar WIDTH in px, centred in each slot. Default: auto — the bar fills
its slot (the band minus the category/bar gaps). Clamped to the slot so it
can't overrun a neighbour.

properties.name: cornerRadius
properties.description: Bar corner radius in pixels.

properties.name: zoom
properties.description:
Interactive zoom over the CATEGORY range — the same "zoom is a view" model
as `md-line-chart`:
  • `inside` — drag horizontally across the plot to zoom into that span of
    bars; double-click the plot to reset.
  • `slider` — a range slider under the plot; drag its thumbs to resize the
    window, or the grip between them to pan it.
  • `both` — both gestures.

`series` / `xAxis` are never mutated: the engine is simply fed the sliced
window, and hover / click / keyboard indices are rebased so consumers still
see ABSOLUTE data indices. Ignored on a `polar` chart (a ring has no span to
zoom). For a *value*-range zoom, set `yAxis.min` / `yAxis.max`.

properties.name: locale
properties.description:
BCP-47 locale for the DEFAULT number / date formatting (axis ticks,
tooltip values, screen-reader table). Empty follows the browser; an
explicit `valueFormatter` always wins.

properties.name: tooltipRenderer
properties.description: Replace the tooltip's content. See `md-line-chart`'s `tooltipRenderer`.

properties.name: noAnimation
properties.description: Disable all animation (shorthand for `animation="none"`).

properties.name: animation
properties.description: Entry-animation variant: `expressive` (default), `grow`, `fade`, `draw`, or `none`.

properties.name: animationDuration
properties.description: Entry-animation duration override in ms (≤ 0 disables).

properties.name: showLabels
properties.description: Show numeric data labels on each bar.

properties.name: showTotals
properties.description:
Print each stack's TOTAL past the end of the column, alongside the
per-segment values `show-labels` prints inside it. Stacked charts only —
an unstacked bar already IS its total.

properties.name: chevron
properties.description:
Draw the bars as CHEVRONS pointing away from the baseline instead of as
rectangles. Along a stack they interlock, each segment's point sitting in
the next one's notch — a force diagram, where the contributions are handed
along in a direction rather than merely piled up.

properties.name: polar
properties.description:
Wrap the bars around a circle: one concentric RING per category, with the
value axis running as an ANGLE instead of a length. A radial (polar) bar
chart.

Stacking, legend hiding and percentage normalisation all work unchanged —
only the step from a value to geometry differs, and the value axis
deliberately spans less than the full circle, since a ring that closes on
itself has no readable start or end. The quarter it gives up is where the
category names go; `polar-sweep` changes how much that is.

properties.name: polarHole
properties.description: Radius of the hole at the centre of a polar chart, 0..0.9. Default 0.22.

properties.name: polarSweep
properties.description: Fraction of the circle the value axis spans on a polar chart. Default 0.75.

properties.name: axisTicks
properties.description: Draw small perpendicular tick marks on the axes.

properties.name: clickable
properties.description:
Show a hand (`pointer`) cursor over the bars, signalling they're actionable —
e.g. clickable to drill into. The chart can't know an interaction is wired,
so set this when a `mdBarClick` handler does something (like `drill`). The
cursor tracks the bar itself (hit-tested like a click), not the empty column
above a short bar.

properties.name: loading

rather than appearing fully formed. Slot `loading` to replace the default
indicator with your own skeleton.

components.name: Button
components.description: A discrete, committed action. Five emphasis levels, five sizes, round/square shape with M3-Expressive shape morphing, optional toggle mode, and native form participation (submit/reset) via ElementInternals.

notes: Dedicated native Button uses source size/density metrics, variant/toggle/disabled color tokens, Roboto and Material Symbols fonts, slot fallback, and source loader placement.

Actual SwiftUI isPressed drives shape morphing (200ms press, 400ms release). Pointer-origin ripple uses source farthest-corner geometry and 450ms growth/150ms fade; hover and pointer geometry are forwarded by the native preview. Reduce Motion suppresses shape/ripple animations. Per-instance source visual hooks are exposed through AWCButtonAppearance rather than CSS execution.

Loading draws the source 48-vertex morphing polygons with the original 4.55s keyframes and easing; Reduce Motion uses the source opacity pulse. Native button groups inject direct child size, shape, toggle and connected corner props; composite-specific neighbor motion is not reproduced. RTL icon mirroring uses native layout direction; expanded trailing-icon rotation requires an explicit aria-expanded property on the native node.

mdClick describes the proposed state before commit and includes value, toggle, selected, href and target; mdChange follows commit and includes selected and value. originalEvent is omitted; activation.source identifies pointer, keyboard, accessibility or unknown native provenance.

AWCButtonAction dispatches actual native capture, target and bubble phases before defaults. preventDefault vetoes activation; stopPropagation retains same-scope listeners and stopImmediatePropagation stops them. Legacy onEvent receives final cancellation, propagationPath and native activation metadata. Native mdChange is noncancelable. Soft-disabled and loading controls keep native keyboard focus while suppressing activation.

type submit/reset uses the nearest AWCFormScope or an explicit owner registry. All 13 source form-control families auto-register with stable per-view identity, ordered successful values and validation. Cancelable mdSubmit/mdReset precede form effects; reset restores initial native bindings (OTP clears). Single-line Enter activates the first registered default submit button. AWCFormEncoding generates local UTF-8 URL-encoded data without network submission. target is passed to AWCURLRouter; raw nonempty href suppresses form actions.

AWCNavigationCoordinator implements local _self/_blank/_parent/_top and named presentation contexts, current-base relative resolution, ordered histories/back and host veto/presentation callbacks. AWCButtonNavigationDemo shows real button propagation controls and local navigation without external page loads. Named reuse is an explicit native policy, not source noopener browser behavior.

groupTabindex implements the source null/0/-1 native focus contract: -1 skips sequential keyboard entry while retaining pointer, programmatic and accessibility actions. Hard-disabled excludes focus; soft-disabled/loading remain focusable and inert. Positive HTML tabindex sorting is not reproduced.

roleOverride supports native button/link/gridcell mappings with safe inference for empty/unknown roles. Gridcell selected state is independent of toggle. AppKit exposes a native actionable cell; UIKit supplies button/selected traits and data-table-cell coordinates through explicit AWCGridCellContext, not arbitrary ARIA roles or a browser calendar grid.

Native responder/accessibility assertions run on macOS. UIKit focus-engine/responder synchronization is implemented against documented iOS 17+ APIs, but this host has no iOS SDK/device to validate hardware keyboard or VoiceOver runtime behavior.

AWCButtonAppearance and View.awcButtonAppearance provide validated native appearance values inherited fieldwise by subtree and overridden locally. These are native visual equivalents; CSS parts/selectors/custom properties remain Web-only. Explicit cornerRadius fixes ordinary states; connected corners take source precedence; custom colors preserve disabled alpha. Nested slotted components may retain their own authored styling.

Width/minWidth/maxWidth/height/minHeight use source border-box sizing with minimum constraints winning conflicts; content remains centered and nowrap, with overflow clipped by the button shape. Typed AWCNode.symbol / AWCMaterialSymbol children inherit icon sizing and color and are decorative by default. A supplied circular indeterminate progress loader keeps its own dimensions.

HTML_FORM.description: Actual native md-button submit/reset and text-field Enter use explicit form owners, all 13 source form-control families, source successful-value rules, ordered entries, validation, cancelable form events and reset bindings. Encoding is local and deterministic.
limitations: This implements the native form contract, not DOM ElementInternals, HTML form attributes, browser validation bubbles, autofill, CSS pseudo-classes or HTTP navigation. Explicit owner IDs resolve through an injected AWCFormRegistry.

ICU patterns and Foundation URL parsing differ from browser JavaScript v-mode regex and URL parsing. UTF-16 length, common email/URL/number constraints, time bounds and native custom validators are supported; HTML dirty-value validity timing and every ValidityState flag are not reproduced.

Implicit submission uses native single-line onSubmit and the first registered default submit button. Source number-field commits then submits directly. Browser composition/deferred autocomplete selection and DOM tree-order algorithms are not emulated.

Source md-button requestSubmit does not contribute a submitter name/value. Native submit(submitter:) can carry explicit host metadata, without adding a source button entry. Native form events are mdSubmit/mdReset/mdInvalid, not browser SubmitEvent/ResetEvent objects.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: Actual md-button activation dispatches scoped native capture, target and bubble listeners with a stable path/target/current scope, explicit boundaries, synchronous cancellation and both propagation stops. Defaults follow accepted mdClick; noncancelable mdChange follows toggle commit. Legacy observations include final cancellation, native activation metadata and path.
limitations: These are explicit native scopes and boundaries, not DOM nodes, browser capture/retargeting, shadow roots or a browser composedPath. Boundary crossing is a native dispatch option; target identity is never silently retargeted.

Activation metadata identifies entry through native control, implicit-submit or programmatic action. It does not fabricate a DOM MouseEvent, raw OS event, modifier/middle-button semantics or browser isTrusted. Finished synchronous contexts cannot be canceled later.

DOM_GLOBAL.description: Observable native contexts resolve safe relative routes against current source history, implement self/blank/parent/top destinations and reusable named contexts, and provide local back navigation. Host approval precedes state changes; presentation callbacks observe committed state. The navigation demo renders local context and history state without external navigation.
limitations: Native contexts replace presentation destinations, not browser window/document objects, browsing-context groups, window.open, opener relationships, referrers, origin security or HTTP page loads. No network request or application launch occurs in the coordinator.

Named destinations are intentionally reusable native contexts. The source browser route uses noopener/noreferrer and may create fresh browsing contexts for named targets. Reserved native targets are case-insensitive; other underscore-prefixed names are rejected.

Relative routes use Foundation URL resolution and explicit native context base URLs; URL parsing is not claimed identical to the browser. Schemes are allowlisted and executable/file/data routes rejected. The default SwiftUI openURL fallback still delegates external presentation to the host and does not interpret browser target contexts.

SHADOW_DOM.description: An explicit native component tree owns nested content and rendering without accessing browser shadow roots.
limitations: This replaces component content ownership; it does not implement CSS shadow-tree encapsulation or DOM retargeting.

DOM_QUERY.description: Typed tree traversal finds native descendants by stable node ID or source tag without querying browser elements.
limitations: Supports explicit native ID/tag lookup, not arbitrary CSS selectors, live DOM collections or imperative HTMLElement references.

SLOT_INTROSPECTION.description: Native named-child lookup and dynamic fallback are used by md-button for default content, leading/trailing icons and loader.
limitations: Operates on declarative native child values; browser assignedElements, slotchange events and flattened DOM slot semantics do not exist.

notes: Native Compose button with explicit forms, cancelable action scopes, safe routing and named content; browser-specific gaps are described in nativeEquivalents.

Dedicated Compose button matches source size/density rules, all five palette/toggle variants, bundled source Roboto and Material Symbols fonts, 200ms press/400ms release corner morph, source pointer-origin ripple timing and polygon loading animation. Real Compose PressInteraction owns press state. Source slots replace icon/label/loader fallbacks. Native form scopes automatically register source field adapters, collect ordered successful entries, apply declarative rules and support vetoable submit/reset and Enter; native action scopes can synchronously cancel defaults or stop scoped propagation; safe application routing carries target metadata. Literal browser form APIs, browser documents/origins, DOM nodes, platform elevation shadows, antialiasing and unrestricted browser ARIA roles remain different. Native groupTabindex supports null/0 sequential entry and -1 omission while preserving native programmatic focus, touch and accessibility actions. Hard-disabled controls are excluded; soft-disabled/loading controls remain focusable and block activation. roleOverride supports button and gridcell; unknown values safely retain Button semantics. Grid cells expose selected state independent of toggle plus explicit AWCGridScope/AWCGridCellScope collection metadata. mdClick reports proposed selected state before commit; mdChange follows commit. DOM originalEvent is omitted. RTL mirroring/expanded rotation currently applies to icon string fallbacks; custom icon slots retain their own transforms. Per-instance CSS custom properties are not evaluated.

HTML_FORM.description: AWC source field adapters register automatically with native form scopes. Shared declarative rules, ordered successful-control entries, duplicate names, multi-values, native Enter/default submission, vetoable submit/reset, initial-state restoration and explicit owner IDs replace the button form contract.
limitations: Native scope ownership replaces ElementInternals; no DOM nodes, browser validation popup or browser network submission is created.
Pattern validation uses Kotlin/Java full-match regular expressions, not the HTML JavaScript v-flag grammar. Native declarative text types cover text, email, URL and number.
Entry order follows native registration order. Applications that reorder retained keyed controls must re-register them when a new data order is required.

SHADOW_DOM.description: Scoped Compose content supplies the button label, leading/trailing icons and loader without a shadow root.
limitations: This is native composition; browser style encapsulation and DOM node access are not exposed.

DOM_QUERY.description: Explicit named-content lookup and injected navigation replace the button-specific anchor and slot queries.
limitations: Arbitrary CSS selectors and DOM traversal are not provided.

SLOT_INTROSPECTION.description: Observable composition replaces slot assignment inspection; adding/removing registered content updates the button and restores absent-slot fallbacks. Legacy content lambdas remain supported.
limitations: Slots contain composables rather than HTMLElement collections. Custom icon content retains its own transforms.

DOM_GLOBAL.description: Safe relative links resolve against the source native context current URL. Observable native contexts implement self, blank, parent, top and reusable named destinations, independent history, back and subtree close. A host can reject navigation before commit and present accepted destinations after commit. Unsafe raw links never fall through to form actions.
limitations: Contexts are native application state, not browser windows, documents, origins or opener relationships; no page is fetched by the coordinator.

Named native destinations are deliberately reusable; source window.open with noopener/noreferrer may instead create fresh browser contexts. Browser modifier/middle-click navigation and window APIs are not reproduced.
URLs must parse as native URIs. Applications supply presentation for coordinator destinations; the legacy default router still opens absolute Android URIs.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: Synchronous native capture, target and bubble dispatch uses stable target/path/scope IDs and ordered listeners. Cancelable mdClick runs before defaults, with separate stopPropagation and stopImmediatePropagation controls; committed mdChange is noncancelable. Explicit boundaries and nonbubbling events are supported; legacy callbacks still observe actions after dispatch.
limitations: The event path contains explicit native scopes, not DOM nodes or browser shadow-tree retargeting.
Activation metadata defaults to unknown when the host cannot identify the source; DOM originalEvent, isTrusted, browser modifiers and cancellation of native OS input are not claimed.

components.name: Button Group
components.description: A set of related buttons that behave as one control. Wraps md-button / md-icon-button children, forces them into toggle mode, and manages selection, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and — in connected mode — the fused container shape.

notes: Dedicated native group layout implements standard/connected source gap and density ladders, source child size/shape/toggle injection, mixed button/icon children, logical connected corners and minimum floors, nowrap overflow, explicit dimensions and min/max precedence. Full-width divides content-box flex basis then adds each child padding/border; text children stretch vertically while icon definite heights remain fixed. Seven public layout hooks map to inherited AWCButtonGroupAppearance points.

Child actions run before independent raw group reconciliation. Single/multi selection, required restoration, duplicate/empty values and previous-event value diffs preserve source ordering. Canceling a child mdClick blocks child actions but does not block the separate raw group click; soft-disabled/loading pointer clicks can still reconcile the group. Hard-disabled controls do not. Group notification cancellation cannot undo already committed child state.

mdSelectionChange carries values, added and removed only. Native activation metadata preserves the initiating pointer/keyboard/accessibility identity; DOM originalEvent objects are not fabricated. There are no source methods or CSS parts. Native named children replace the structural default slot.

Source-ordered roving focus supports RTL Left/Right, Home/End, selected/recent-focus fallback and hard-disabled skipping. Nested groups forward focus/key/raw-selection actions through their parent chain. Native accessibility exposes a containing group and each real child button selected/disabled state; DOM ARIA strings are not executed.

Standard neighbor motion uses the source per-side size ladder, 150ms peak and 400ms completion, while connected corners override child radius hooks. Required selected children suppress motion. Listener eligibility follows the initial source variant, including connected-to-standard no-motion behavior. Reduce Motion suppresses animation.

Live/Snapshot hosts accept buttonGroupAppearanceDefaults/buttonGroupAppearance and buttonGroupSelection in authored descendant order. Live captured frames return exact ordered child booleans independently of value strings, retaining duplicate/empty identities. Group pointer down/up/move/cancel and normal native keyboard input are supported.

Checked-in source-contract and actual SwiftUI geometry/event/focus/pointer/motion fixtures plus live JSON protocol verification cover this component. Only macOS SwiftUI/AppKit was compiled and executed here; iOS SDK/device/VoiceOver validation remains unavailable. See audits/md-button-group.md.

Native nowrap layout with source density gaps, connected mixed-button corners, content-box flex sizing, seven typed layout hooks, standard neighbor press motion, ordered selection snapshots and roving focus. Raw click reconciliation runs after child behavior even when child action was canceled or soft-disabled/loading; required can reselect the clicked child. The group emits once per raw click, including unchanged deltas. Nested and wrapped descendants participate in every ancestor group, with shared selected state, inner-to-outer raw-click reconciliation and authored-tree focus order. DOM originalEvent is replaced by actual child activation metadata, not fabricated.

DOM_QUERY.description: Native authored layout-tree traversal includes nested and wrapped descendants; shared selection and inner-to-outer reconciliation preserve ancestor participation. Logical layout direction and roving keyboard focus replace DOM queries.
limitations: Native layout-tree traversal replaces querySelectorAll; arbitrary CSS selector evaluation is not exposed.

DOM_OBSERVER.description: Native button and icon-button children register in measured composition order and retain state across keyed reordering.

CSS_RUNTIME.description: Typed native appearance, density and child layout metrics provide the gap, geometry and neighbor-press motion inputs that the Web component reads from computed CSS.
limitations: Arbitrary CSS rules are not evaluated by the native renderer.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: mdSelectionChange is dispatched through native action scopes after selection is reconciled, with values, added and removed arrays and actual child activation metadata. Cancellation does not reverse the already committed selection, matching the Web event order.
limitations: Native scope propagation replaces DOM bubbling and composed paths; a browser originalEvent object is not fabricated.

properties.name: appearance
properties.description:
Surface style of the chip. Distinct from `variant`, which selects the M3
chip TYPE (assist / filter / input / suggestion); a chip has both.

- `outlined` (default) — transparent container with a 1px outline.
- `filled` — tonal container, no outline.
- `elevated` — tonal container with elevation and no outline.

properties.name: color
properties.description:
Colour role applied to the chip's outline / label / container, depending on
`appearance`. Omit for the neutral surface treatment.

Any role name the THEME defines is accepted, not just a fixed list — the
chip resolves `<name>` to the `--md-sys-color-<name>` /
`-<name>-container` / `-on-<name>-container` family at runtime. So
`color="brand"` works as soon as a theme ships those tokens, and a name the
theme does not define degrades to the neutral treatment rather than
rendering broken.

`primary` | `secondary` | `tertiary` | `error` are the baseline M3 roles;
`success` | `warning` | `info` ship in packages/tokens on the same tonal
recipe. The union below is a hint for editor autocomplete only — the `string`
arm is what makes custom roles work.

properties.name: elevated
properties.description: Whether the chip is elevated (adds shadow instead of outline).

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Disables the chip

properties.name: softDisabled
properties.description: Soft-disabled: disabled visuals but remains focusable

properties.name: removable
properties.description:
When `true`, the chip renders a trailing remove ("✕") button and responds
to Delete / Backspace from the chip itself. Works on every variant.

`variant="input"` is removable by default (per MD3 spec) — setting
`removable="false"` explicitly opts out of that behavior.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Label text — alternative to default slot

properties.name: contentAlign
properties.description:
Inline-axis alignment of the chip's content row — leading icon, label and
trailing icon together.

`center` (the default) is a no-op on a normal chip, which shrink-wraps its
label: the content box and the container are the same size, so there is
nothing to align. It matters only once a layout gives the chip a width — a
grid column, `align-self: stretch`, an explicit `inline-size` — and then
centre is usually wrong. The label floats in the middle of a wide outlined
box and reads as an empty input rather than a chip, and a chip labelling
something beneath it no longer shares a left edge with what it names.

`start` reads left in LTR / right in RTL, `end` the reverse, `center` is
direction-agnostic. Use `::part(label)` for finer control.

inherited one. 0 = default, -4 = ultra-compact.

components.name: FAB
components.description: The single most prominent action on a screen. Floats above the UI in seven color mappings and three sizes, and morphs between an icon-only circle and an extended pill that carries a label.

notes: Dedicated SwiftUI FAB implements all three icon-only sizes, seven source palettes, five density rungs and lowered/hover/focus/pressed elevation. Any nonempty label uses the standard extended geometry; actual natural Roboto text measurement drives the source spatial/opacity transition, and collapsed labelled FABs retain minimum width56 at every density. Oversized explicit icons stay centered before clipping.

Native pointer, Enter/Space keydown and accessibility activation emit one cancelable scoped mdClick. Detail is null because the source DOM MouseEvent has no native object equivalent; public event.activation supplies truthful native ID/source. There is no selected payload, toggle, navigation or mdChange side effect. Hard-disabled excludes focus; soft-disabled remains focusable and inert. Authored aria-label or label supplies the native accessible name; decorative Material glyph names are not spoken.

AWCNode.symbol(name, slot: "icon") uses the bundled Material font at resolved iconSize. AWCNode.slotText creates element-like authored content, including empty/whitespace, and literal text inherits host typography/letter spacing independently of glyph size. Temporary icon overrides suppress slots without modifying authored children. Native children support arbitrary reusable composition; browser slot nodes are not executed.

Attach a retained AWCFabController using View.awcFabController. Its async setMenuIcon(String?) accepts nonempty whitespace without trimming; nil or empty clears the temporary override and reveals the latest authored icon/slot. It remains callable while disabled. Live preview invokes the real controller before command completion; FAB Menu manages its own separate anchor morph lifecycle.

All five public appearance hooks map to validated AWCFabAppearance fields with scoped fieldwise inheritance. Container disabled precedence follows source CSS, while explicit inner iconColor/labelColor still win. The three visual parts have measured native inspector counterparts; arbitrary CSS selector execution remains a Web API.

Passed141 shared FAB metric/palette/slot contracts and94 actual offscreen SwiftUI geometry/pixel/interaction/controller checks, plus the real JSON live-host method test. Library and all preview products compile on macOS. This machine has Command Line Tools only; iOS SDK/device/VoiceOver runtime remains unverified. See audits/md-fab.md.

The icon slot retains authored content during controller overrides. mdClick callback detail is null in place of a DOM MouseEvent; scoped AWCActionEvent detail is an empty map and truthful input metadata is available through activation. components.name: FAB Menu
components.description: A FAB that fans out into 2–6 related actions. Anchors to an existing md-fab by id, morphs that FAB's icon to close while open, and manages the popup's ARIA wiring, roving focus, and dismissal.

notes: Dedicated anchored menu uses public AWCFabMenuScope with separate authored native anchor and menu nodes. Actual native frames drive up/down/auto positioning, RTL alignment and moving-anchor tracking; no synthetic anchor, scrim or fabricated item list is added by the renderer. The preview composes a real extended FAB with three authored items in a 360 by 480 point context.

Retain AWCFabMenuController and attach View.awcFabMenuController. Async show waits for actual native initialization, close begins the 180 ms closing phase, and whenClosed waits for the closed render. Reopen cancels closing without losing the current cycle waiter; detach resolves lifecycle waits. Initial open mounts silently. Live method IDs use bounded retention, idempotent acceptance, explicit terminal queries and completion independent of visual streaming.

Anchor pointer/Enter/Space capture suppresses its own action before opening. Fresh pointer opening keeps anchor focus; keyboard or already-focused pointer opening enters the first item. Native roving focus includes disabled items while blocking their activation. Arrow, Home/End, Tab/Shift-Tab, Escape and printable typeahead use actual native focus. Outside clicks include the containing native window outside the authored scope.

Three typed appearance fields cascade into actual item renderers; native density inheritance preserves source missing/zero behavior and local negative overrides. Anchor FAB reuses its public temporary icon controller, preserves extended label geometry, and applies ellipse, source icon rotation/scale/fade and vibrant colors. Scoped authored appearance is restored after close rather than destroying immutable values to reproduce Web inline-style cleanup.

Focused controller, actual AppKit/SwiftUI layout/pixel/interaction and live-host protocol fixtures are wired into existing native runners. macOS validation is recorded in audits/md-fab-menu.md. This environment has no iOS SDK/device runtime; UIKit and VoiceOver execution is not claimed.

Native nonmodal FAB menu uses AWCFabMenuScope with separately authored ID anchors, actual native bounds, a retained item tree and scoped controller show/close/whenClosed lifecycle. Source input ordering, roving focus, typeahead and typed appearance are implemented; runtime acceptance is recorded separately in audits/md-fab-menu.md. AWCSlotText or AWCSearchableLabelScope supplies actual searchable names for arbitrary native label content. Native scoped appearance restores authored FAB colors on close rather than deleting immutable authored appearance as Web inline-style cleanup does.

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: A common action expressed as an icon alone. Four emphasis styles, five sizes, three container widths, round/square shape with shape morphing, and an optional toggle mode with a distinct selected glyph.

notes: Dedicated SwiftUI icon-button implements the source 5 sizes, 3 widths and 5 density rungs, 4 variant palettes including toggle/selected/disabled precedence, bundled Material Symbols, shape morphing and logical connected corners. It shares the tested native focus/responder and pointer-origin ripple infrastructure with md-button.

Default/selected named children obey meaningful-content fallback: raw whitespace and md-badge do not mask the icon prop; AWCNode.slotText creates an authored element-like wrapper, including an explicit empty wrapper, and AWCNode.symbol uses the real Material font. Selected glyphs swap only in selected toggle mode; selected palette/morph also applies without toggle. Avatar children retain their own size; badge adornments anchor to the physical top-right of the icon wrapper and may overflow the host.

AWCIconButtonAction preserves source navigation, then toggle commit, then mdClick({selected}) ordering. The event supports native scoped capture/target/bubble and cancellation metadata, but canceling this post-action notification cannot undo navigation or selection. There is no mdChange, source imperative method, or form-submit behavior. Native activation.source identifies pointer, keyboard, accessibility or unknown entry.

Enter/Space activate on keydown with a 150ms press pulse; pointer press holds until release/cancel. Hard-disabled excludes focus; soft-disabled remains focusable and inert. groupTabindex implements ordinary/null, 0 and -1 native focus semantics. Positive browser tabindex ordering is not emulated. aria-label supplies the authored native accessible name; decorative Material glyph names are not spoken. Source role remains button even when href is present.

Target is supplied to AWCURLRouter; AWCNavigationCoordinator can provide explicit self/blank/parent/top/named native presentation contexts. It does not create browser windows, opener/referrer behavior or DOM events. Relative routes require a host base URL. The default SwiftUI openURL fallback delegates presentation to the app.

Nine public visual hooks map to validated AWCIconButtonAppearance values inherited fieldwise through View.awcIconButtonAppearance. All three CSS parts have measured native visual counterparts; arbitrary CSS selectors and CSS execution remain Web APIs. Corner radius overrides resting shape, while selected/pressed morph targets and connected corner precedence follow the source.

Actual NSHostingView geometry, palette pixels, slot updates, pointer, keyboard, native focus and accessibility are covered by a checked-in test runner. macOS SwiftUI library/live/snapshot products compile and run. This environment has Command Line Tools only; iOS SDK/device/VoiceOver execution is unverified. See audits/md-icon-button.md.

Dedicated Compose renderer implements all 19 source properties, all five size and density rungs, narrow/default/wide widths, four source palettes, selected/pressed/resting morph precedence, connected logical corners, pointer-origin ripple, keyboard focus and native group coordination. Default/selected slots replace glyph fallbacks; direct native badges adorn without suppressing the icon and avatars retain their own dimensions. Navigation and toggle commit before cancelable mdClick notification, exactly as the source does; no mdChange is emitted. The nine public CSS hooks map to AWCIconButtonAppearance. Native layout evidence covers the visual root, state-layer and active icon part. Source DOM objects, CSS selector evaluation, browser windows and forced-colors media queries remain platform-specific.

SHADOW_DOM.description: Default and selected composable slots replace source glyphs. Direct native badges and avatars preserve their source slot sizing roles.
limitations: Native composition replaces shadow DOM; arbitrary DOM inspection is not exposed.

DOM_QUERY.description: Native slot lookup and injected application routing replace the component-specific DOM queries.
limitations: No arbitrary CSS selector engine or browser window is created.

SLOT_INTROSPECTION.description: Subcomposition detects actual child layout and selects the default or selected icon layer; badges do not count as replacement icons. Explicit Text composables, including empty editor text, represent authored replacement elements.
limitations: Compose children replace DOM nodes; omission restores fallback while an authored empty element suppresses it.

DOM_GLOBAL.description: Safe relative links resolve against the source native context current URL. Observable native contexts implement self, blank, parent, top and reusable named destinations, independent history, back and subtree close. A host can reject navigation before commit and present accepted destinations after commit. Unsafe raw links never fall through to form actions.
limitations: Contexts are native application state, not browser windows, documents, origins or opener relationships; no page is fetched by the coordinator.

Named native destinations are deliberately reusable; source window.open with noopener/noreferrer may instead create fresh browser contexts. Browser modifier/middle-click navigation and window APIs are not reproduced.
URLs must parse as native URIs. Applications supply presentation for coordinator destinations; the legacy default router still opens absolute Android URIs.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: Scoped native capture/target/bubble delivery exposes cancelable mdClick after safe navigation and selection have already committed, matching the source icon-button ordering.
limitations: Calling preventDefault marks the notification but cannot undo effects that preceded it. OS input and DOM propagation are not fabricated.

properties.name: series
properties.description:
Series array. Each entry is one line. Empty → empty state.

`data` is either a bare list of y values, positioned by index against
`xAxis.data`, or a list of points carrying their own x —
`{ x: '2021-11-13', y: 0.12 }` / `['2021-11-13', 0.12]`. Points are what
irregular data needs: uneven sampling, or several series measured on
completely different dates. Set `xAxis.scale = 'time'` (or `'value'`) so
the gaps render proportionally; series carrying their own x need no
`xAxis.data` at all.

properties.description: X-axis configuration.

properties.description:
Multiple independent value (y) axes. When set (non-empty), each series is
measured against `yAxes[series.yAxisIndex ?? 0]`, and the axes stack outward
from the plot (first → left, rest → right, or per each axis' `position`).
Supersedes the single `yAxis`. Each axis keeps its own `min`/`max`/`scale`/
`valueFormatter`/`label`.

properties.name: curve
properties.description: Default curve interpolation. Overridable per-series.

properties.name: stack
properties.description: Stacking strategy.

properties.name: connectNulls
properties.description: Whether `null` values are bridged with a straight line.

properties.name: showMarks
properties.description: Show data-point markers on every series by default.

properties.name: lineWidth
properties.description:
Line stroke width in px, for every series. Default 2.5; a per-series
`series[].lineWidth` overrides it.

properties.name: markSize
properties.description:
Marker RADIUS in px, for every series. Overrides the per-symbol default; a
per-series `series[].markSize` wins.

properties.name: area
properties.description: Render the line area as a filled gradient below the line.

properties.name: showLine
properties.description:
Draw the line for each series. Default `true`. Set `false` for a fill-only
chart (with `area`) or a marks-only chart — handy when a high `fillOpacity`
makes the same-coloured line vanish into the fill. A per-series
`series[].stroke` still wins over this.

properties.name: legend
properties.description: Legend position. `'none'` hides the legend.

properties.name: tooltip
properties.description: Tooltip interaction model.

properties.name: grid
properties.description: Gridlines: horizontal (y ticks), vertical (x ticks), both, or none.

properties.name: axisTicks
properties.description: Draw small perpendicular tick marks on the axes.

properties.name: inverted
properties.description:
Transpose the axes — the x-axis data runs vertically and the values run
horizontally (e.g. a temperature-by-altitude spline). Best with `curve="smooth"`.

properties.name: showLabels
properties.description: Print each point's value as a data label beside its marker.

properties.name: seriesLabels
properties.description: Label each series at its last point with its name (follows the line end).

properties.name: zoom
properties.description:
Interactive zoom over the x range.
  • `inside` — drag horizontally across the plot to zoom into that span;
    double-click anywhere in the plot to reset.
  • `slider` — an `md-slider` in range mode under the plot: drag either
    thumb to resize the window, click the track to jump the nearest thumb,
    drag the window itself to pan. Thumbs are focusable and take
    Arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown.
  • `both` — both of the above.

Zoom is a *view* over the data: `series`/`xAxis` are untouched, and
`mdHover`/`mdMarkerClick` keep reporting absolute indices into your data.

BCP-47 locale for the DEFAULT number / date formatting — axis ticks,
tooltip values and the screen-reader table. Empty follows the browser.
An explicit `valueFormatter` / `xAxis.valueFormatter` always wins, so a
consumer that formats its own values is unaffected.

properties.description:
Text shown when there is no data. The `empty` slot still overrides it —
this is the prop form, for handing a string straight from a dictionary.

properties.default: 'Chart data. Use the arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for the first and last, Escape to leave.'
properties.defaultValue: Chart data. Use the arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for the first and last, Escape to leave.

properties.name: labelZoomEnd

Replaces the generated `aria-label` outright. The default summary is

properties.name: valueFormatter
properties.description:
Format raw Y values for tooltips / a11y table.

The tooltip also asks it about series with NO value at the hovered x —
`null` when the series has a null datum there, `undefined` when it has no
datum at all. Return `''` (or leave those cases unhandled) to keep the
default behaviour of omitting the series; return a string to show a row
for it — e.g. `(v) => (v === null ? 'no reading' : v === undefined ? '—' : v + ' m')`.

properties.name: tooltipRenderer

Replace the tooltip's content with your own. Receives everything the chart
knows about the hovered x — the axis value + its formatted label, and per
visible series the index, label, colour, raw and formatted value, and
whether it is the emphasised one — split into `series` (has a reading here)
and `missing` (does not).

string (inserted as TEXT, never parsed as markup), `{ unsafeHtml }` to opt

for no tooltip at this x. The engine keeps positioning it, and it is still
the `tooltip` CSS part.

properties.name: listStyle
properties.description:
Visual style of the list.

- `standard` (default, M3 Expressive): rows share a single rounded
  chassis with **no gap** between them. The first row rounds its
  top corners, the last rounds its bottom corners, and middle rows
  are square so the stack reads as one continuous shape — the M3
  "connected" pattern. Best for settings panels, option groups,
  and iOS-style sectioned tables. To add hairline separators
  between rows, interleave `<md-divider>` elements.
- `segmented` (M3 Expressive): rows are individually rounded "tiles"
  separated by a small gap. Each tile rounds all four corners. Best
  for action sets, quick-action menus, and card-like sections where
  each row should read as its own affordance.

properties.name: selectionMode
properties.description:
Selection coordination across child rows.

- `none` (default): each row stands alone and the container is always
  `role="list"` (rows are `listitem`s). Interactive rows (`type="button"` /
  `type="link"`) expose their widget role on an inner primary element, so
  the list validly owns only `listitem`s while still providing the same
  roving-tabindex + arrow-key navigation. `type="text"` rows stay
  non-focusable.
- `single-select`: the container behaves as `role="listbox"`, items
  become `role="option"`, and exactly one item carries `aria-selected`.
- `multi-select`: same as above plus `aria-multiselectable="true"`.

Switching to a selection mode also auto-promotes plain `type="text"`
rows to focusable so users can pick from a list of label-only rows
without authoring extra props.

properties.name: interactionMode
properties.description:
Row interaction pattern for the whole list. A list uses exactly one
interaction mode at a time (per the M3 Lists spec).

- `single-action` (default): each row is one tappable area — leading
  icon + label activate together. Use `type="button"` (or selection
  mode) on items.
- `multi-action`: rows expose a primary action (the row body) plus
  optional secondary actions in `slot="trailing"` (e.g. `md-icon-button`).
  Clicks on trailing controls do not activate the primary row action;
  each secondary control keeps its own focus stop and keyboard behavior.

components.name: List
components.description: A vertical set of related rows. It owns the container role and selection. Roving focus, arrow-key and typeahead navigation, and optional drag-to-reorder are all coordinated here on behalf of its md-list-item children.

notes: Dedicated native list: all eight properties (list, listbox with single/multi selection, menu and other role overrides, density 0…−4), mdSelect, mdActivate and mdReorder with the source payloads (item references become stable native node IDs), the four methods through AWCListController, ten appearance hooks and the drop-placeholder part.

Roving focus with wrap, Home/End and 500 ms typeahead; pointer reorder from the drag handle (lift, sibling shift, dashed placeholder glide, drop) and Alt+Arrow keyboard reorder, measured against Chrome frame by frame.
A reorder keeps the authored composition and translates rows to their displayed slots; on Compose the accessibility order follows the authored order until the host applies mdReorder.

properties.name: type
properties.description:
Behavior of the row.

- `text` (default): non-interactive content row. No focus, no ripple,
  no click event. Use for static labels and section headers.
- `button`: focusable, ripples, fires `mdClick` on activation.
- `link`: same as `button` but also navigates to `href` in `target`.

When the row sits inside an `md-list` with `selection-mode` set, the
row becomes focusable + clickable regardless of `type` so users can
pick from a list of plain rows without authoring extra props.

properties.name: headline
properties.description: Headline text. Overridden by `slot="headline"`.

properties.name: overline
properties.description: Overline text shown above the headline. Overridden by `slot="overline"`.

properties.name: supportingText
properties.description: Supporting text below the headline. Overridden by `slot="supporting-text"`.

properties.name: trailingSupportingText
properties.description: Trailing supporting text on the right. Overridden by `slot="trailing-supporting-text"`.

properties.name: leadingIcon
properties.description: Material Symbols name for the leading slot (24 dp container, 18 dp icon).

properties.name: trailingIcon
properties.description: Material Symbols name for the trailing slot (24 dp icon).

properties.name: leadingAvatar
properties.description:
Avatar image URL — forwarded to an internal `md-avatar` rendered in
the leading slot. Falls back to `leadingAvatarName` / `leadingAvatarLabel`
if the image fails to load.

properties.name: leadingAvatarAlt
properties.description: Alt text for `leadingAvatar`. Also surfaced as the avatar's accessible label.

properties.name: leadingAvatarName
properties.description:
Full name forwarded to the internal `md-avatar` so it can auto-derive
initials when no image is available (`"Ada Lovelace"` → `"AL"`).
When both this and `leadingAvatarLabel` are empty the avatar falls
back to a `person` icon.

properties.name: leadingAvatarLabel
properties.description:
Explicit initials shown by the internal `md-avatar`. Overrides the
`leadingAvatarName` parsing. Used for "C", "JD" style labels.

properties.name: leadingImage
properties.description: Image thumbnail URL (56 dp square by default).

properties.name: leadingImageAlt
properties.description: Alt text for `leadingImage`.

properties.name: lines
properties.description:
Number of text rows. Auto-detected when 1 + content suggests more
(overline → 2-line, overline + supporting → 3-line). Set explicitly
to override the auto-promotion.

properties.name: href
properties.description: Link href. Honored when `type='link'`.

properties.name: target
properties.description: Link target. Honored when `type='link'`.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Disables interaction, removes from tab order, and dims content to 38 % opacity.

properties.name: softDisabled
properties.description: Visually disabled but remains focusable for discoverability. Does not emit activation events.

properties.name: selected
properties.description: Selected state. Toggled by `md-list` when `selection-mode` is on.

properties.name: expandable
properties.description:
Turns the row into a single-level collapsible disclosure. When `true`:
  - a trailing **`md-icon-button`** caret renders after any author-supplied
    trailing content. It is the disclosure control: it carries
    `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls`, gets the icon-button pill/squircle
    shape morph when selected (expanded), and its `expand_more` glyph
    rotates 180° (points up) when expanded.
  - the `expanded-content` slot reveals one level of flat `md-list-item`
    child rows (not a nested `md-list` chassis) inline below the parent
    with an MD3 expressive open (emphasized-decelerate) / retract
    (emphasized-accelerate) height + opacity animation.
  - clicking the row body also toggles the panel as a convenience; the
    caret button additionally toggles on Enter / Space when focused.
  - ArrowRight expands, ArrowLeft collapses (when the row itself is
    focusable, e.g. `type="button"` / reorderable rows).

properties.name: expanded
properties.description: Reflects/controls the expanded state of an `expandable` row.

properties.name: tabbable
properties.description:
Whether this item is the currently tabbable one in its parent list.
Managed by `md-list`'s roving tabindex. Standalone items leave this
as `true` and become focusable when `type !== 'text'`.

properties.name: rovingFocusVisible
properties.description:
When `true`, paints the keyboard-focus ring even if the row does not
hold DOM focus (e.g. toolbar buttons drove `activateNext()`). Set
imperatively by `md-list` during programmatic / arrow-key navigation —
not on initial load.

properties.name: selectionMode
properties.description:
Selection mode propagated from parent `md-list`. Set imperatively by
the parent — authors should not need to touch this directly. When
non-`none`, the item becomes focusable + clickable regardless of
`type` and renders with `role="option"` + `aria-selected`.

properties.name: interactionMode
properties.description:
Interaction mode propagated from parent `md-list`. Set imperatively by
the parent — authors should not need to touch this directly.

- `single-action`: the whole row is one primary action.
- `multi-action`: trailing slot may host secondary controls (icon
  buttons, switches) that keep their own focus/click semantics.

properties.name: containerRole
properties.description:
The resolved ARIA role of the parent `md-list` container, propagated
imperatively by that parent — authors should not touch this. It lets a row
adapt its own role to its container: when the container is a `menu` /
`menubar` (via `role-override`) an interactive row exposes `role="menuitem"`
on the HOST itself (the host IS the widget, like `option`) and skips the
inner primary widget, because a `menu` owns its direct light-DOM children
(the hosts) and must own `menuitem`s — a `listitem` / `role="none"` host is a
disallowed menu child (axe `aria-required-children`). Empty for a plain
`list` / `listbox`, where the default `listitem` / `option` roles apply.

properties.name: reorderable
properties.description:
Whether this row can be reordered via drag-and-drop. Set imperatively by
the parent `md-list[reorderable]` — authors should not need to touch this
directly. When `true` the row renders a trailing drag handle (grab it to
drag) and supports `Alt + ArrowUp / ArrowDown` to move when focused.
Disabled rows ignore it.

properties.name: density
properties.description:
Local density rung. Drives the same `--md-sys-density-scale` signal that a
global `data-density` ancestor sets, so a local value simply overrides the
inherited one. 0 = default, -4 = ultra-compact.

components.name: Loading Indicator
components.description: The M3 Expressive loading moment. A morphing-shape indicator for indeterminate waits — distinct from a progress indicator, which reports how far along something is.

notes: Dedicated native morph renderer uses the exact seven 48-vertex polygons, rounded keyframe offsets, 4550ms cycle, cubic overshoot and rotation from Web. Native reduced-motion becomes the source 2s circle opacity pulse; native increased contrast maps to system semantic foreground/surface. Label is a named indeterminate progress semantic, not visible text.

All five appearance hooks support inherited fieldwise defaults/local overrides, RGBA, intentional zero sizes and structured physical/elliptical/percentage corner radii. AWCLoadingIndicatorShapeAppearance independently overrides the actual exposed shape width, height and color. Finite extreme radius coefficients use overflow-safe proportional CSS overlap normalization.

Actual SwiftUI/AppKit fixture passed 1798 checks across 84 hydrated Web theme configurations and 16 paused animation samples, plus real animation/focus/accessibility/hide transitions. Native inspection reports actual root and shape geometry, including zero, and clears hidden nodes. iOS SDK/device validation is unavailable; platform boundaries and host evidence are recorded in audits/md-loading-indicator.md.

Dedicated native polygon animation preserves source geometry, colors, density, clipping, exact keyframes and typed corner radii. AWCLoadingIndicatorShapeAppearanceScope styles the measured shape part. Android animation preference supplies reduced motion; explicit AWCAccessibilityAppearanceScope forcedColors is a native environment override, not inferred from system contrast. No default tabstop is added; caller focus modifiers opt into native focus. Runtime verification is recorded separately.

properties.name: open
properties.description: Whether the menu is open.

properties.name: anchor
properties.description: ID of the anchor element to position relative to.

properties.name: placement
properties.description: Position of the menu relative to the anchor.

properties.name: quick
properties.description: Skip open/close animation.

properties.name: variant
properties.description:
Visual variant.
- 'baseline': MD3 baseline menu (square corners, surface container)
- 'standard': M3 Expressive vertical menu (rounded, surface-based colors)
- 'vibrant': M3 Expressive vertical menu (rounded, tertiary-based colors)

properties.name: layout
properties.description: Layout style for vertical menus. 'standard' is flat, 'grouped' uses visual section separators.

properties.name: useGap
properties.description: Use gap separators instead of dividers between groups (vertical menu only).

properties.name: emptyText
properties.description: Message shown when all menu items are hidden (e.g. no filter results). Empty string disables.

properties.name: matchAnchorWidth
properties.description: When true, the menu surface min-width matches the anchor element's width. The menu still grows wider if items need more space.

properties.name: responsive
properties.description:
Adapt to compact viewports. The menu is *always* clamped within the
viewport (it never overflows the screen and pins to the edges with a
margin). When `responsive` is set, on viewports at or below the compact
breakpoint (600px) the menu additionally expands to near-full-width
below the trigger for comfortable touch use.

properties.name: persistent
properties.description:
When set, the menu does NOT auto-dismiss in response to interaction
elsewhere on the page. By default a menu closes when:
  1. The user clicks outside the menu and its anchor.
  2. Another non-persistent menu opens (single-open coordination —
     opening menu B closes menu A so two top-level menus never
     overlap each other on screen).

`persistent` opts out of both auto-dismiss paths. The menu then only
closes via `close()`, the anchor's toggle, item activation, or
Escape. Useful for modal-style pickers, multi-step menus, and any
context where the consumer manages dismissal explicitly.

Submenus (an `<md-menu>` rendered inside a parent menu's `submenu`
slot) are never affected by sibling-menu dismissal even without this
flag — ancestors and descendants are always preserved.

properties.name: autoFocus
properties.description:
When false, opening the menu initializes roving tabindex without moving
focus to the first item. The consumer handles focus (e.g. docked pickers
that scroll to the selected option). `show({ autoFocus: false })` still
takes precedence for a single open.

properties.name: maxHeight
properties.description:
Cap the menu surface block-size. When the items exceed it the list
scrolls vertically inside a plain scroll viewport. A number is treated
as pixels; any CSS length is passed through (e.g. `'50vh'`). Unset, the
cap falls back to `--md-menu-max-block-size` (250px). Applies to menus
with submenus too: their flyouts are `position: fixed` and escape the
scroll viewport rather than being clipped by it.

properties.name: listbox
properties.description:
Present the popup as a WAI-ARIA listbox (surface `role="presentation"`,
anchor `aria-haspopup="listbox"`) rather than a menu. `md-select` sets this
for both its virtual and non-virtual lists so the popup is a listbox of
options regardless of size. (The virtual path additionally registers a
provider, which adds the aria-activedescendant focus model.)

properties.name: density
properties.description:
Local density rung. Drives the same `--md-sys-density-scale` signal that a
global `data-density` ancestor sets, so a local value simply overrides the
inherited one. 0 = default, -4 = ultra-compact.

cssProperties.name: --md-menu-max-block-size
cssProperties.description: Max height before the list scrolls (default 250px);

cssProperties.name: --md-menu-inline-fill-radius-end
cssProperties.description: Bottom corner radius for inline-fill embed (default 0)

it as a property, not an attribute). When provided, the CLAMPED value is
formatted with it (`{ style: 'unit', unit: 'gigabyte' }`, currency, plain
number…). When omitted, the value's position in the range is formatted as
a locale-aware percentage — the default, because a meter answers "how
full", which a bare number cannot say without its bounds alongside it.

properties.name: color
properties.description:
Colour role applied to the fill and track. Any role name the THEME defines
is accepted, not just the listed ones — the meter resolves `<name>` to the
`--md-sys-color-<name>` / `-<name>-container` pair at runtime, so
`color="brand"` works as soon as a theme ships those tokens.

The default (`primary`) keeps md-progress-indicator's neutral look:
primary fill on a secondary-container track. Every other role paints
`<role>` fill on a `<role>-container` track.

properties.name: variant
properties.description:
Shape of the reading.

- `linear` (default) — a horizontal bar, full width of its container.
- `circular` — a ring. `show-value` puts the value in the middle of it and
  `show-label` captions it underneath, instead of the bar's header row.

The ring does NOT mirror under `dir="rtl"`: it fills clockwise in every
locale, matching Material's circular progress (and a clock face).

properties.name: size
properties.description:
Ring diameter in dp — circular only, ignored by the bar. Clamped to
24…240 like md-progress-indicator, and tapered by density through the
`--md-meter-size` hook.

properties.name: thickness
properties.description: Track thickness in dp. Density-scaled (0.5px per rung), floored at 2px.

properties.name: density
properties.description:
Local density rung. Drives the same `--md-sys-density-scale` signal that a
global `data-density` ancestor sets, so a local value simply overrides the
inherited one. 0 = default, -4 = ultra-compact.

components.name: Meter
components.description: A read-only graphical display of a numeric value within a known range. Storage used, quota consumed, password strength, battery level. role="meter" with the full ARIA value contract on the host, value clamping, Intl-driven formatting (locale-aware percent by default), and MD3 semantic status colors.

notes: Dedicated read-only native Meter implements bounded finite ranges, extreme-range overflow protection, linear/circular geometry, density, RTL, actual named level semantics, source line boxes and timed value/opacity transitions. There are no source events, slots or methods.

Public AWCMeterFormatter uses data-only system JavaScriptCore Intl.NumberFormat with omitted-versus-empty options preserved, raw-number fallback for invalid locale/options, and signed-zero-safe caching. Intl option and locale data follow the installed Apple OS. Arbitrary case-sensitive theme color roles and RGBA values are retained; seven sparse appearance fields merge inherited defaults and local overrides.

Actual macOS SwiftUI/AppKit fixture passed2669 checks across196 hydrated Web theme configurations, including108 independent formatting cases and real motion, RTL text, native semantics, hidden and zero geometry. Five parts report actual layout; circular track/indicator bounds describe paths rather than stroke extents. iOS SDK/device execution is unavailable; see audits/md-meter.md for precise evidence and platform boundaries.

Dedicated read-only Compose meter supports the fourteen source properties, native ICU locale formatting and seven typed appearance hooks. AWCMeterRangeKey retains the exact Double range alongside Android accessibility range data. Native paths, shaped text and measured visual parts replace SVG and CSS. Runtime verification is recorded separately in the parity audit.

nested / modal-docked layouts. Set this when the rail is the app's

components.name: OTP Field
components.description: One-time-code entry. Renders length real cells in its own shadow root (it owns the inputs, so every cell carries full ARIA), routes all entry — typing, paste, SMS autofill — through one sanitizing pipeline, and participates in forms via ElementInternals with the full constraint-validation API. No hidden input, no wrapper md-text-field.

notes: Dedicated native OTP field (SwiftUI on AppKit / UIKit inputs, Compose BasicTextField): one real input per character with the source's single pipeline — strip whitespace → transform → validation-type filter → clamp — for typing, paste, autofill bursts and programmatic writes; the contiguous value model; groups with the separator slot; mask; density 0…−4; seven hooks.

Keyboard: Backspace clears the cell (or the previous one from an empty cell), Delete removes the character at the cell, ←/→/Home/End move between cells, every cell is a Tab stop, Enter submits the form; a paste anywhere replaces the whole code from cell 0; mdInput, mdChange (on completion and when focus leaves the group), mdComplete (a complete paste re-announces it), mdInvalidInput with the rejected text, mdValidityChange; auto-submit requests the form submission after mdComplete.

Methods through AWCOTPFieldController: setFocus() (first empty cell), clear() (silent), getValidity / setCustomValidity / checkValidity / reportValidity (customError, valueMissing with valueMissingLabel or incompleteLabel).
Forms: the code is the form value; an empty code submits no entry; reset clears it. Cell 0 carries the one-time-code content type (SMS autofill).

macOS SwiftUI, the iOS simulator and the Android emulator are verified against Chrome 153 (paint, per-frame border motion, events). iOS has no pointer hover (touch), so the hover outline does not apply there.

properties.name: monochrome
properties.description:
Render every slice as a shade of ONE colour instead of the categorical
palette — darkest first, lightening around the ring.

Worth reaching for when the slices are ordered (a ranking, a funnel) rather
than merely different: a single hue stops the reader hunting for meaning in
colour that isn't there, and it survives most colour-vision deficiencies,
which a five-hue palette does not.

Takes an MD3 role or any CSS colour. Present with no value (`monochrome`)
uses `primary`; absent means off — so an explicit empty string is the
"on, with the default" case rather than an accident.
